speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; to help me understand what is causing this, can you tell me if you have been passing gas or having bowel movements normally?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is fussy, feeding poorly, and has worsening pain when the abdomen is touched, along with visible distension. Did you notice any episodes of forceful, projectile vomiting, especially in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No projectile vomiting or signs of infection are present. Given the distension, pain on palpation, and lack of bowel movements mentioned earlier, have you noticed if the baby has passed any stool since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis
